newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Gasoline firms, naphtha quiet.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Gasoline firms, naphtha quiet.

text.p: Gasoline traders lifted prices higher on Tuesday with active bids and offers and one 95-octane deal was done as players returned to the market after the long weekend holiday, traders said.
But talks in the naphtha market remained thin as the Japanese market was still on holiday, they added.
The 50,000-barrel 95-octane deal was traded at $27.30 lifting March 1-5 from an European major to a U.S. major.
"The market is quite active today with increased trading interest after the holiday," said one trader.
On Thursday, 95-octane was traded at $26.80 per barrel lifting February 21-25 between a Dutch trader and a U.S. major.

Unleaded 92-octane gasoline was bid at $27.00 per barrel in late Tuesday trade, compared with an earlier offer of $26.90. The cargoes were for differing dates. Gasoline 97-octane was bid at $28/$28.20, traders said.
Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) announced on Thursday a tender to buy 250,000 barrels of 95-octane unleaded reformate for March 16-30.
The CPC tender closes on February 18 and is valid until February 20.
Naphtha February swaps weakened to $23.70/$24.20 per barrel from Thursday's late bid of $24.50/$24.90 and March swaps were also down to $23.40/23.90 from $24.20/$24.60.
"With Japanese players still having a holiday, nothing is going on in the naphtha market," said a major.
"We have to wait until tomorrow to see activity after all the players return to the market," he added.
